reading.body:
The Centersquare Chicago facility publishes 147.6 MW of utility power across 237,000 square feet of technical space, enough for roughly 3,700 racks at typical AI training density.

Centersquare operates 80 data centers across 15 North American markets claiming more than 500 MW total capacity. The Chicago facility holds security certifications for regulated financial, healthcare, and US government workloads, which limits its fungibility for commercial AI training but signals buildout for high-assurance compute. The operator's portfolio footprint matters for grid pressure because if the 500 MW claim is accurate, a single private operator controls meaningful regional power in multiple markets simultaneously.

A critical gap undermines any read of this facility's actual role in AI scaling. The operator publishes two different power figures for the same site: 147.6 MW in one location and 32.8 MW in another. The corresponding floor space figures do not reconcile either. Without third-party grid data or physical verification, it is impossible to determine whether this campus ranks among the largest compute buildouts in Illinois or among the smaller ones. This data shows that operator-published capacity figures remain unverified in real time, which matters because AI scaling constraints depend on actual grid load, not claimed nameplate.
